frequency_question: How often does structural friction prevent the successful signing of a successor treaty within the required window?
membership_rule: Includes major bilateral river water sharing treaties globally that reached expiration and required formal renegotiation within a 36-month window; excludes domestic water disputes and non-treaty unilateral extractions.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty permanent arbitration/modification attempts

provenance_note: claimed 2 hits but 3 of 5 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 5 named cases representing major transboundary water treaty renewals under structural friction; estimated roughly 8 comparable instances globally in the modern era.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unpublicized bilateral river arrangements in Central Asia and Africa due to lack of verifiable structured data on friction points.
skeleton: Global instances of expiring bilateral water treaties where sub-national or structural veto friction applied during renewal windows
multiplier: 2 successful renewals / 5 identified major negotiations where structural friction was prominent
validity_reason: International water diplomacy norms and structural bureaucratic frameworks remain stable over a 4-to-5-year horizon.
